summary: Adds a Flask search blueprint and a config file with a Stripe key, and changes /items pagination. It also downgrades lodash, loosens the Dockerfile, and edits the deploy script and CI workflow.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: The search_items function puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. Any quote in q changes the query. Any caller of /search can read every table in items.db. The same caller can also change or delete data in it. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a ? placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: The search_items function puts the q request parameter straight into the SQL text with an f-string. Any quote in q changes the query.
findings.consequence: Any caller of /search can read every table in items.db. The same caller can also change or delete data in it.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a ? placeholder.

findings.title: Stripe secret key committed to source
findings.description: The config file hardcodes a Stripe API key as a string literal. The key now lives in the git history. Anyone with read access to the repository can make payment API calls as the shop. Revoke the key in Stripe and read the new key from an environment variable or a secret store.
findings.problem: The config file hardcodes a Stripe API key as a string literal. The key now lives in the git history.
findings.consequence: Anyone with read access to the repository can make payment API calls as the shop.
findings.fix: Revoke the key in Stripe and read the new key from an environment variable or a secret store.

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.description: The list_items function now computes offset as page * PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0. No client can ever fetch the first 20 items. Every page shows the rows the next page should show. Restore the offset as (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE.
findings.problem: The list_items function now computes offset as page * PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20 instead of row 0.
findings.consequence: No client can ever fetch the first 20 items. Every page shows the rows the next page should show.

findings.title: Lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change moves lodash from 4.18.1 back to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws. Front-end code that calls the affected lodash functions with untrusted input is exposed to these known exploits. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.
findings.problem: The change moves lodash from 4.18.1 back to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that calls the affected lodash functions with untrusted input is exposed to these known exploits.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.description: The change removed the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask process now runs as root inside the container. A code execution bug in the app gives the attacker root inside the container. The new search injection is one such path. Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before CMD.
findings.problem: The change removed the app user and the USER 10001 line. The Flask process now runs as root inside the container.
findings.consequence: A code execution bug in the app gives the attacker root inside the container. The new search injection is one such path.
findings.fix: Restore the useradd step and the USER 10001 line before CMD.

findings.title: Base image pinned to latest
findings.description: The change replaced the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm image with python:latest. Every build can now pull a different Python version. A new Python major or minor release can break the image without any code change, and builds become irreproducible. Pin the base image to an explicit version tag again.
findings.problem: The change replaced the pinned python:3.12.7-slim-bookworm image with python:latest. Every build can now pull a different Python version.
findings.consequence: A new Python major or minor release can break the image without any code change, and builds become irreproducible.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to an explicit version tag again.

findings.title: Package install can stop at a confirmation prompt
findings.description: The apt-get install command runs without -y. Apt stops whenever it needs to install or upgrade a package. The image build fails as soon as a curl update or a missing dependency needs installing. Add -y and --no-install-recommends to apt-get install, and clear the apt lists afterwards.
findings.suggested_change: RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
findings.problem: The apt-get install command runs without -y. Apt stops whenever it needs to install or upgrade a package.
findings.consequence: The image build fails as soon as a curl update or a missing dependency needs installing.
findings.fix: Add -y and --no-install-recommends to apt-get install, and clear the apt lists afterwards.

findings.title: Pull request title expanded inside a shell command
findings.description: The new step puts the pull request title straight into the run script. A title with shell syntax runs as a command on the runner. Any pull request author can run commands in CI just by choosing a title. Pass the title through an env entry and quote the variable in the script.
findings.problem: The new step puts the pull request title straight into the run script. A title with shell syntax runs as a command on the runner.
findings.consequence: Any pull request author can run commands in CI just by choosing a title.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env entry and quote the variable in the script.

findings.title: Unquoted deploy directory in rm -rf
findings.description: The rm -rf command now uses DEPLOY_DIR unquoted. Spaces or glob characters in the value split it into several paths. A DEPLOY_DIR such as /srv/my demo makes the script delete /srv/my and ./demo instead of the deploy directory. Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.
findings.problem: The rm -rf command now uses DEPLOY_DIR unquoted. Spaces or glob characters in the value split it into several paths.
findings.consequence: A DEPLOY_DIR such as /srv/my demo makes the script delete /srv/my and ./demo instead of the deploy directory.
findings.fix: Quote the variable and keep the non-empty guard.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.description: The loop now splits unquoted ls output on whitespace. It also prints bare names instead of the full paths the old glob printed. File names with spaces show up as several bogus entries in the deploy log. Restore the quoted glob loop.
findings.problem: The loop now splits unquoted ls output on whitespace. It also prints bare names instead of the full paths the old glob printed.
findings.consequence: File names with spaces show up as several bogus entries in the deploy log.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no covering test
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint or the changed list_items offset. The injection flaw and the pagination regression both shipped without any test catching them. Add tests for /search with quote characters and for /items page 1 returning the first rows.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search_items endpoint or the changed list_items offset.
findings.consequence: The injection flaw and the pagination regression both shipped without any test catching them.
findings.fix: Add tests for /search with quote characters and for /items page 1 returning the first rows.

candidate.message: Using variable interpolation `${{...}}` with `github` context data in a `run:` step could allow an attacker to inject their own code into the runner. This would allow them to steal secrets and code. `github` context data can have arbitrary user input and should be treated as untrusted. Instead, use an intermediate environment variable with `env:` to store the data and use the environment variable in the `run:` script. Be sure to use double-quotes the environment variable, like this: "$ENVVAR".

candidate.message: Avoiding SQL string concatenation: untrusted input concatenated with raw SQL query can result in SQL Injection. In order to execute raw query safely, prepared statement should be used. SQLAlchemy provides TextualSQL to easily used prepared statement with named parameters. For complex SQL composition, use SQL Expression Language or Schema Definition Language. In most cases, SQLAlchemy ORM will be a better option.

candidate.message: Detected user input used to manually construct a SQL string. This is usually bad practice because manual construction could accidentally result in a SQL injection. An attacker could use a SQL injection to steal or modify contents of the database. Instead, use a parameterized query which is available by default in most database engines. Alternatively, consider using the Django object-relational mappers (ORM) instead of raw SQL queries.
